justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift over time, starting near 73.8 for the one-day horizon and gradually rising to 75.5 at one month. The one-day estimate is anchored heavily to recent price action and momentum — whatever the asset was trading at recently, short-term mean reversion and intraday continuity tend to dominate, so I expected little movement from the prevailing level. The one-week estimate nudges slightly higher, incorporating a mild positive trend assumption and the likelihood that any near-term catalysts would resolve constructively. The one-month estimate extends that drift further, reflecting a base case where underlying fundamentals or macro conditions provide a gentle tailwind, though the confidence in that direction weakens considerably at longer horizons.

The width of my confidence intervals expands substantially as the time horizon lengthens, which reflects the fundamental reality that uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 6.6 units, consistent with typical daily volatility and the limited time for new information to accumulate. By one week, the interval nearly doubles to 13 units, capturing the possibility of scheduled data releases, central bank communications, or sector-specific news that could shift sentiment meaningfully. At one month, the interval widens to 25 units, acknowledging that over four weeks, an entirely different macro narrative could emerge, earnings could surprise significantly, or liquidity conditions could shift in ways that are genuinely difficult to anticipate from the current vantage point.

There are several tail risks that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals entirely. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macro conditions — such as an unexpected credit event, a sharp policy reversal, or a geopolitical shock — could drive prices well below 70.5, even within a single day. A liquidity crunch or forced de-leveraging in related markets could amplify any initial move. On the upside, a surprise positive catalyst such as a major policy stimulus announcement, a blowout earnings report, or a resolution of an ongoing geopolitical tension could push prices above 81 within a week or beyond 88 within a month. These tail scenarios are individually unlikely but collectively represent meaningful probability mass that the intervals are designed to capture only partially — by construction, roughly 10% of outcomes are expected to fall outside the stated bounds.
